summary.en-US: YouTube's speed keys jump by 0.25x and, without Premium, stop at 2x. This keeps the same keys and removes the limit, with smaller steps where you want them: 2.1x, 2.2x, 2.3x. Adds a speed button to the player and Shorts. Collects no data.

description.en-US:
I watch lectures and talks at around 2.3x. Without Premium, YouTube stops at 2x, and its speed keys move a quarter at a time: 1.75x, 2x, done. So I made this.

It keeps YouTube's own speed keys and takes the cap off. Above 2x the steps get smaller, 0.1x by default, because that's where a small change decides whether you keep up with the speaker or lose them.

**What it does**

- Speeds from 0.25x to 4x out of the box: 0.25x steps up to 2x, then 0.1x steps.
- Shift + . is faster, Shift + , is slower, R jumps between 1x and your speed.
- A speed button in the player, next to YouTube's own controls. Scroll over it to change speed, or click it for a slider and presets. On Shorts it sits with the top-right controls.
- Hold the mouse button down on the video for twice your speed, up to your fastest setting. Let go and you're back. At 1.5x, holding gives you 3x.
- Your speed stays put across videos, ads, tabs and restarts.

**One speed control**

YouTube resets the speed on every new video and ad. The extension sets yours back every time. That also means YouTube's own speed menu can't change it. If you pick a speed there, a bubble shows the speed you're actually at.

Another speed add-on can't change it either, and if it keeps trying, the two undo each other. Turn the other one off for YouTube.

**Your own steps**

Open the settings from the player panel without leaving the video, or from the toolbar button. You can set:

- where the step size changes, 2x by default
- the step size below and above that speed, as fine as 0.01x
- the slowest and fastest speed, anywhere from 0.1x to 16x
- up to 8 preset buttons

Slowing down works the same way. For language practice or learning a song, move the step change to 1x and set the step below it to 0.05x. Firefox keeps voices at their normal pitch.

**Limits**

- It works on www.youtube.com in desktop Firefox 142 and newer.
- Not supported: YouTube Music, m.youtube.com, Firefox for Android, and YouTube videos embedded on other sites.
- At the live edge of a live stream it leaves the speed to YouTube, because there's nothing ahead to speed through. Go back a bit and your speed applies again.
- Firefox mutes the sound above 8x. You can raise that limit in about:config. The settings page shows how once you set Fastest above 8x.

**Privacy**

No accounts, no analytics, no network requests. The extension only has access to youtube.com. It stores your speed and settings in your Firefox profile. On YouTube pages it adds about 35 KB of code, unminified. The source is on GitHub: https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube

Not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

release_notes.en-US:
- Hold the mouse button down on the video to play at twice your speed, up to your fastest setting. This replaces YouTube's own hold, which always gives 2x.
- If you pick a speed in YouTube's own menu, a bubble shows the speed you're actually at.
- Speed keys no longer change your speed on pages without a video.
- Full settings open in the top-right corner, like the toolbar popup, without dimming the video. A click outside closes them without pausing the video.
- Reset and preset removals can be undone for 5 seconds.
- Presets outside your range are kept and come back when you widen it.
- Keyboard and screen reader support in the player panel.
- The welcome page now explains how it all works. The hint in the player is gone.
- Fixed: a − or + button could move a value the wrong way, and clearing a field reset it to the default.

Full list: https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

version.approval_notes: No build step or minification: the submitted files are the source, also at https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube. To test, open any youtube.com/watch page and press Shift+. a few times, or click the speed button at the start of the player's right-hand controls. The tune icon in that panel opens options.html in an iframe over the page (declared in web_accessible_resources); the content script accepts messages only from that iframe's window and the extension's origin, and the iframe posts only to https://www.youtube.com. background.js opens welcome.html once, on first install, and on update removes two storage keys that older versions left behind. The settings footer links to this add-on's AMO page. To try hold for double, hold the left mouse button on the playing video. While the extension runs, a speed picked in YouTube's own menu is put back on purpose. No remote code and no network requests. The UI is built with DOM calls, no innerHTML.
